real_basis.note: on this row the basis is 'no' (free delivery stated only over GBP 50, listing is GBP 20.22). The field IS read: stripping it changes the reason from DELIVERY_COST_NOT_SUPPLIED to DELIVERY_BASIS_NOT_STATED. The row stays ineligible either way because a 'no' needs a delivered cost, and no cost was read into a numeric field.

verdict: The mapping is wired. With the delivery basis stated and a price the basis covers, the row is eligible; stripped it drops out on DELIVERY_BASIS_NOT_STATED; restored it is eligible again. On the real U26 rows the field is read too (the reason code moves between DELIVERY_BASIS_NOT_STATED and DELIVERY_COST_NOT_SUPPLIED), but no harvested UK page states delivery-included, so no real row becomes eligible — the real rows are blocked on DELIVERY_COST_NOT_SUPPLIED (a stated threshold the price fails) or on a silent page.
